The counterpart has played ACTION_Y (YIELD) 2 times out of 5 rounds (40%).

- Rate 3: 0.3

We calculate the likelihood of observing 2 Ys in 5 trials for each rate using the binomial formula $P(k|n,p) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}$:
- Rate 1 (0.9): $\binom{5}{2} (0.9)^2 (0.1)^3 = 10 \times 0.81 \times 0.001 = 0.0081$
- Rate 2 (0.7): $\binom{5}{2} (0.7)^2 (0.3)^3 = 10 \times 0.49 \times 0.027 = 0.1323$
- Rate 3 (0.3): $\binom{5}{2} (0.3)^2 (0.7)^3 = 10 \times 0.09 \times 0.343 = 0.3087$
- Rate 4 (0.1): $\binom{5}{2} (0.1)^2 (0.9)^3 = 10 \times 0.01 \times 0.729 = 0.0729$

The most likely rate is Rate 3 (0.3), followed by Rate 2 (0.7).
To find the expected probability $P(Y)$, we sum $(Rate \times Likelihood) / \sum Likelihoods$:
$\sum Likelihoods = 0.0081 + 0.1323 + 0.3087 + 0.0729 = 0.522$
$E[P(Y)] = \frac{(0.9 \times 0.0081) + (0.7 \times 0.1323) + (0.3 \times 0.3087) + (0.1 \times 0.0729)}{0.522}$
$E[P(Y)] = \frac{0.00729 + 0.09261 + 0.09261 + 0.00729}{0.522} = \frac{0.1998}{0.522} \approx 0.3827$

**Step 3: Determine optimal action**
Expected Value of ACTION_X (DARE): $4 \times P(Y) + 0 \times P(X) = 4 \times 0.3827 = 1.5308$
Expected Value of ACTION_Y (YIELD): $3 \times P(Y) + 1 \times P(X) = 3 \times 0.3827 + 1 \times (1 - 0.3827) = 1.1481 + 0.6173 = 1.7654$

Since $1.7654 > 1.5308$, ACTION_Y (YIELD) is the optimal choice.
